prediction_scored: miss. Registered: cool half-year rate ratio 0.95 to 0.99 per +5 C. Found 1.002 (0.993 to 1.012); the interval includes 1 and lies above the whole registered range. Secondary (moderator) prediction: warm-minus-cool difference of log rate ratios positive; found 0.0093 (-0.0118 to 0.0305), right sign, interval includes 0: not met.
settle: Asthma emergency visits by day and age group from the Health Department's syndromic system, which is not on NYC Open Data, with a distributed-lag model to 21 days as in the Hong Kong and Hefei studies, and daily pollen and ozone. The EMS series bounds the within-month effect of a cold day within four days at under 1% per 5 C in either direction, and the sign changes under other time controls (see notes); it cannot see a three-week lag through month fixed effects.

notes:
Deviation from the registration: the asthma call types first appear on 2006-09-28, so the series starts 2006-10-01, not 2006-01-01. 326,660 dispatches on 7,275 days. Warm half-year rate ratio 1.012 (0.993 to 1.032). Sensitivity analyses (final call type, lag 0, lags 0-7, minimum temperature, excluding March 2020 to June 2021) all give cool-season rate ratios between 1.001 and 1.006 with intervals including 1. Exploratory, by calendar month: June 1.064, July 1.132 (1.079 to 1.187), August 1.080, September 0.899 (0.869 to 0.931), February 0.963 (0.937 to 0.990). The September slope is confounded with the date: asthma rises after schools open while days cool, and month fixed effects do not remove a trend inside a month. The half-year split chosen at registration averages a positive summer slope with this negative September one.

After the referee (13 Nov 2026): the bound in the outcome applies to variation within a calendar month at lags of up to four days, and not generally. The sign of the cool-season slope depends on how time is controlled: with year effects and four annual harmonics it is 0.985 (0.972 to 0.9985), which would have met the support condition, and with year-month effects and lags 0 to 21 it is 1.027 (1.006 to 1.049). Neither was registered and neither changes the verdict. The named alternative that asthma calls are absorbed by difficulty-breathing codes on cold days was tested by the referee and does not hide a cold effect: those codes rise with temperature in the cool half-year (1.0125, 1.0055 to 1.0196). Asthma dispatches fell from about 24,000 a year in 2014 to about 9,000 in 2024, which may reflect a change in call typing; the slope is the same before and after 2013. On the graph side, PMID 35817164 supplies several rows that are strata of one analysis (2.16 is the relative risk on days with high PM2.5 and 1.64 on days with low PM2.5), so '16 of 17 findings' overstates the number of independent results and '7 studies' is the better count.

critique.answer: accepted; verdict kept, scope of the bound stated
